title: Marketplace local legal & data residency — onboarding notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes to capture the legal and data residency requirements that need to be surfaced in marketplace listing copy, the partner onboarding checklist, and the technical acceptance gates. This is a pragmatic doc for launch-readiness conversations with Legal, Security, and Marketplace product managers.

Scope / audience:
- Audience: internal GTM, listings team, partner integrations squad, legal review.
- Scope: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listings across NA/EU/APAC where data residency requirements vary. Not a final legal brief — high-level copy + acceptance criteria + edge cases.

Key constraints we need to call out in listing copy (short snippets below):
- Data residency: customers in regulated industries ask about where inference inputs/outputs and logs are stored. Must call out region and retention policy.
- KMS & keys: whether customer-managed keys (CMK) are supported or platform-managed keys.
- Audit logs: retention windows and availability to customers.
- Private deployments: VPC/on-prem options and their limitations (no cross-region replication by default).
- Third-party subprocessors: list of major cloud sub-processors and link to DPA.

Acceptance checklist (for listing to be allowed to go live):
- [ ] Legal sign-off on DPA copy (CON-4321).
- [ ] Security: threat model for per-tenant isolation and KV cache deletion documented (JIRA-ML-781).
- [ ] Engineering: clear statement of which telemetry is collected and how long it is retained.
- [ ] PM: marketplace tile copy includes explicit region/residency statement.
- [ ] Ops: runbook for customer requests to purge data in 72 hours tested.
- [ ] Sales: standardized response template for RFPs regarding residency and compliance.

Listing copy snippets (aim for short, clear, marketplace tile / short description voice):
- Tile headline: "Predictable LLM inference with region‑bound data control"
- 1-line summary: "Run production LLM inference with options for region-based data residency, CMK support, and private VPC deployments."
- Short benefit bullet: "Keep customer data in the cloud region you choose — no cross-region replication unless explicitly enabled."
- Compliance callout (short): "Supports audit logs, SOC 2 controls, and customer-managed keys for regulated deployments. Contact sales for on‑prem options."

Longer listing paragraph (for marketplace detail section):
"Redwood Inference provides a unified inference platform designed for production workloads. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployment modes and control where your request payloads and logs reside. We integrate with cloud KMS for customer-managed encryption keys and offer audit logs with configurable retention. For regulated workloads, ask about VPC/on-prem packaging and regional deployments to meet data residency requirements."

Onboarding & technical gates (integration team checklist):
- Pre-integration: confirm customer region requirements and enterprise contract terms.
- Deployment options matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs private, and expected impact on latency/cost.
- Security inputs required from partner before listing: SAQ, penetration test summary, subprocessor list.
- Verify: CMK support lane exists and documented (if not, fallback copy must be clear).
- Verify: telemetry endpoints and sample logs are scrubbed for PII by default.

Edge cases & gotchas (notes to self):
- Some marketplaces block the phrase "does not transfer data out of region" — prefer "keeps data in the chosen region unless explicitly enabled".
- On Azure marketplace, need to align to their TM6 data flow diagram format — ask infra for diagram export.
- If customer requests deletion within X hours, ops needs a documented workflow; currently we have a 72-hour validated path for Dedicated customers only.
- On-prem packaging: legal requires SC product security questionnaire completed before packaging.

Draft responses for sales / partner Qs (quick snippets):
Q: Where is customer data stored?
A: By default, payloads and logs are stored in the cloud region selected during provisioning. For Dedicated and Private deployments you can pin region or run on-prem. We also offer data retention controls and CMK integration. (link to DPA)

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
A: Yes — CMK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments on supported cloud providers. Hosted API with CMK is available via enterprise contract (contact solutions engineering).

Outstanding questions to resolve with Legal/Security:
- Do we need a separate short-form residency statement per cloud vendor? (asked Legal 2026-01-14)
- Exact telemetry retention windows to state publicly (security to confirm by 2026-02-28).
- Are any of our subprocessors considered "international" transfers that require special language for APAC markets?

References & links:
- CON-4321 (DPA draft)
- JIRA-ML-781 (telemetry disposition tasks)
- Slack thread: #marketplace-listings – thread ts 1640000000000

Decision log (quick):
- 2025-11-20: decide to surface "region-based data control" on tile instead of absolute guarantees. Owner: Ava.
- 2025-12-08: PM asked to include CMK callout in short bullets — accepted.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Ava: finalize short tile copy + hand to design for tile approval (due 2026-02-05).
- Miguel: get infra diagram export for Azure marketplace (due 2026-01-28).
- Priya: coordinate Legal language for APAC transfers (due 2026-02-10).
- Samir: test ops purge workflow for Dedicated customers (due 2026-02-18).

Open ideas / experiments for copy testing:
- A/B test tile with "region-bound" vs "region-aware" phrasing for conversion impact.
- Track support ticket frequency for residency questions before/after making copy changes.

Notes to self: keep this doc as the single source for short copy variants and the acceptance checklist. Once Legal signs DPA and Security confirms telemetry windows, promote a cleaned final copy to "marketplace-listing-copy-final.json" in the same folder.

-- end --
